==English== ===Etymology 1=== ====Proper noun==== {{en-proper noun}} # {{lb|en|chiefly|Christian Science}} [[God]]. #* {{RQ:Tennyson In Memoriam|XXXII|51|Then one deep love doth supersede
⁠All other, when her ardent gaze
⁠Roves from the living brother’s face,
And rests upon the '''Life''' indeed.}} # {{lb|en|cellular automata}} Conway's [[Game of Life]]. #* {{quote-newsgroup|en|date=1999-05-13|author=Thomas Womack|title=3D automata with Life-style objects|newsgroup=comp.theory.cell-automata|url=https://groups.google.com/g/comp.theory.cell-automata/c/Ad1jbW4rOEU/m/cF_BbefM4AQJ|text=Is there a known 3D totalistic or semi-totalistic automaton ('''Life''' is the latter sort - state at time t+1 depends on state at time t and count of neighbours) which exhibits the same sort of behaviour as '''Life''' (that is, a reasonable range of naturally-occuring{{sic}} still lives and short-period oscillators)?}} =====Derived terms===== * [[Highlife]] * [[Life-like cellular automaton]] * [[Life without Death]] ===Etymology 2=== Variant of {{m|en|Leaf}}. ====Proper noun==== {{en-proper noun|s}} # {{surname|en}}. =====Statistics===== * According to the 2010 United States Census, ''Life'' is the 37591st most common surname in the United States, belonging to 592 individuals. ''Life'' is most common among White (79.73%) and Black/African American (13.51%) individuals. ===Further reading=== * {{R:en:DAFN}} ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=efil|File|flie|filé|elif|lief|Fiel|file}}
